<note>The author refers to the "Goetic" arts, or low magic involving the summoning of spirits.</note> can be easily called out from the body, as the practitioners of Goetia teach. Indeed, even the magi and necromancers <note>Those who communicate with the dead.</note> claim that this can be achieved through certain natural forces and bonds, just as we discuss in our own books on *Occult Philosophy*. For this reason, the ancient fathers, who were skilled in spiritual matters, ordained—not without cause—that the bodies of the dead should be buried in a sacred place, accompanied by lights, sprinkled with holy water, perfumed with frankincense and incense, and purified with prayers for as long as they remain above the earth. 

For as the masters of the Hebrews <note>Referring to Kabbalistic or Jewish mystical traditions.</note> say, our entire body and the carnal animal—and whatever in us rests upon the poorly disposed matter of the flesh—is left as food for the serpent, and for him whom they call Azazel <note>original: "Azazeli"; a demon or spirit associated with the wilderness and the scapegoat in Leviticus.</note>, who is the lord of flesh and blood and the prince of this world. In the book of Leviticus, he is called the prince of the deserts, to whom it was said in Genesis: *You shall eat the earth all the days of your life.* And in Isaiah: *Dust shall be your bread.* This means our body, created from the dust of the earth, remains his so long as it has not been sanctified and transformed into something better, so that it is no longer the serpent’s but has become God’s—namely, changed from carnal to spiritual. This follows the word of Paul who says: *What is sown is a natural body, it rises a spiritual body.* <note>1 Corinthians 15:44</note> And elsewhere: *We shall all indeed rise, but we shall not all be changed,* because many are destined to remain forever as food for the serpent. 

Therefore, we lay down this foul and horrid matter of the flesh and the serpent’s food at death, intending to take it up again one day when it has been transformed into a better and spiritual lot, which will occur at the resurrection of the dead. This has already happened in those who have tasted the first fruits of the resurrection; many have attained this very thing by the power of the deifying spirit in this life, such as Enoch, Elijah, and Moses. Their bodies, transformed into a spiritual nature, did not see corruption, nor were they left to the power of the serpent like other corpses. This is the meaning of that dispute between the devil and Michael over the body of Moses, which Jude mentions in his epistle. But enough has been said of Goetia and Necromancy.

### ON THEURGY.

Most people consider Theurgy <note>term: Theurgy; literally "god-working," a form of high magic aimed at union with the divine or summoning benevolent spirits.</note> to be not at all unlawful, as if it were governed by good angels and the divine power. However, it is very often bound up with the evil deceptions of demons under the names of God and angels. For we win over and attract the celestial powers—and through them, the divine virtues—not only by natural forces but also by specific rites and ceremonies. The ancient magi treat these in many rules published in their volumes. 

The greatest part of all these ceremonies consists in observing cleanliness: first of the mind, then also of the body and those things surrounding the body, such as the skin, clothes, dwellings, vessels, utensils, offerings, victims, and sacrifices. The cleanliness of these things prepares one for the familiarity and contemplation of divine beings and is urgently required in sacred acts, according to the words of Isaiah: *Wash yourselves and be clean, and take away the evil of your thoughts.* Impurity, because it frequently infects both the air and the person, disturbs that most pure influx of celestial and divine things, and [drives away] the pure spirits of God...

# ON THE KABBALAH.

<note>original: "DE CABALA"</note>

Truly, sometimes unclean spirits and deceptive powers, in order to be worshipped and adored as gods, also demand this purity; therefore, there is a need here for the greatest caution, concerning which we have discoursed at length in our books on *Occult Philosophy*. <note>The author refers to his own famous work, *De Occulta Philosophia libri tres*.</note> However, Porphyry <note>A Neoplatonist philosopher who wrote on theurgy and the soul.</note>, disputing many things about this theurgy <term>theurgy: a form of high magic intended to invoke the presence of gods or spirits</term>, or divine magic, finally concludes that by theurgic consecrations the soul of a man can indeed be rendered fit for the reception of spirits and angels, and for seeing the gods; but he utterly denies that a return to God can be provided by this art. Of that school, therefore, are the art of the Almadel, the Notary art, the Pauline art, the art of revelations, and many such superstitions, which are all the more pernicious because they appear more divine to the unskillful.

### ON THE KABBALAH.

<image-desc>Decorative initial V featuring a landscape with a building and foliage.</image-desc>
But here the words of Pliny <note>Pliny the Elder, Roman naturalist and author.</note> occur to me, who says there is also another faction of magic, depending even now upon Moses and Jotopea <note>likely a corruption of Jochabed or a reference to a legendary Jewish magician</note> among the Jews. These words remind me of the Kabbalah of the Jews, which is a firm opinion among the Hebrews was given by God himself to Moses on Mount Sinai, and thereafter through successive stages without written monuments, was handed down to posterity by the living voice alone until the times of Ezra. Just as the Pythagorean dogmas were formerly handed down by Archippus and Lysis, who held schools at Thebes in Greece, in which the disciples, holding the precepts of the teachers by heart, used their intellect and memory instead of books; so also certain Jews, having scorned letters, placed this in memory, observation, and vocal tradition. Whence it is called "Kabbalah" by the Hebrews, as if it were the reception of one from another by hearing alone. It is (as they say) an ancient art, but the name was not known among Christians until recent times. <margin>Kabbalah is twofold.</margin> Indeed, they hand down a twofold science of it: one concerning *Bereshit* <note>original: "Bresith" - the first word of Genesis, meaning "In the beginning"</note>, which they also call cosmology, namely, explaining the powers of natural and celestial created things, and expounding the secrets of the Law and the Bible by philosophical reasons. This, in truth, differs in no way by this reasoning from natural magic, in which we believe King Solomon excelled. For it is read in the sacred histories of the Hebrews that he used to discourse from the cedar of Lebanon even unto the hyssop; likewise of beasts, birds, creeping things, and fishes, all of which can display certain magical powers of nature. Moses the Egyptian <note>Maimonides, the famous Jewish philosopher.</note> himself also, among the later ones, followed this in his expositions upon the Pentateuch, as did many Talmudists. But the other science they call *Merkavah* <note>original: "Mercaua" - referring to the "Chariot" mysticism of Ezekiel</note>, which is concerning the more sublime contemplations of divine and angelic virtues, and of sacred names and seals; a kind of symbolic theology, as it were, in which letters, numbers, figures, things and names, and the tips of elements, and lines, points, and accents, are all significative of the most profound things and great secrets. This again they cut into two parts: into Arithmancy <note>divination by numbers</note>, namely that which is called *Notaricon* <note>a Kabbalistic method of forming new words from the initials or finals of others</note>, treating of angelic virtues, names, and seals, and even the conditions of demons and souls; and into Theomancy, which searches out the mysteries of the divine majesty, emanations, sacred names, and pentacles. He who knows this, they say, is powerful with wonderful virtues, so that when he wishes he may foreknow all future things, command all nature, and [rule] over demons...

# ON THE CABALA
-> G iiii <-

...that he might have power over demons and angels, and perform miracles. By this art, they believe **Moses** performed so many signs: turning his staff into a serpent, and the waters into blood; sending frogs, flies, lice, locusts, caterpillars, fire with hail, blisters, and pestilence upon the **Egyptians**; slaying every firstborn from man even unto beast; and leading his people out, opening the sea, bringing forth a spring from the rock, and quails from heaven; sweetening bitter waters; sending before his people lightning and clouds by day, and a column of fire by night; calling down the voice of the living God from the heavens to the people; striking the arrogant with fire and the murmurers with leprosy; afflicting the undeserving with sudden slaughter, while others were swallowed by the gaping of the earth; feeding the people with celestial food; appeasing serpents; healing the poisoned; preserving a vast multitude from infirmity and their garments from wearing away; and rendering them victorious over their enemies. Finally, by this art of miracles, **Joshua** commanded the sun to stand still, **Elijah** called down fire from heaven upon his adversaries and restored a dead boy to life, **Daniel** bound the mouths of lions, and the three boys sang songs in the furnace of glowing fire. Furthermore, the faithless **Jews** assert that by this art even **Christ** performed such admirable things so often; and that **Solomon** also mastered it, and from it handed down an art against demons—their bonds and methods of incantation—and charms against diseases, as **Josephus** <note>Flavius Josephus, a 1st-century Romano-Jewish historian.</note> testifies. 

But while I do not doubt that God revealed to **Moses** and the other prophets many mysteries contained beneath the "husk" <note>original: "sub cortice" - a common metaphor for the hidden spiritual meaning beneath the literal text.</note> of the words of the Law, which were not to be communicated to the profane masses, yet this art of Cabala which the **Hebrews** boast of—and which I once scrutinized with much labor—I recognize as nothing but a mere rhapsody of superstition and a kind of theurgic magic <note>Theurgy refers to rituals intended to invoke the presence of or cooperate with divine spirits or deities.</note>. For if (as the **Jews** boast) it proceeded from God for the perfection of life, the salvation of men, the worship of God, and the understanding of truth, surely that Spirit of Truth—who came to teach us all truth after the Synagogue was rejected—would not have hidden this from His Church until these final times. For the Church surely knows all things that are of God, whose blessing, baptism, and other revealed sacraments of salvation are perfected in every language. For the power of each and every language is equal and the same, provided the piety is equal and the same; nor is there any other name in heaven or on earth in which we must be saved, and in which we may work virtue, except the one name of **Jesus**, in whom all things are recapitulated and contained. Hence the **Jews**, though most expert in the divine names, can perform little or nothing after **Christ**, unlike their ancient fathers. 

As for what we experience and see in the "revolutions" <note>A technical term in Cabala for the permutation and combination of letters.</note> of this art (as they call it), where wondrous sentences of great mysteries are often wrung from the sacred scriptures, all of this is nothing other than a certain play of allegories. Idle men, occupied with individual letters, points, and numbers—which this language and style of writing easily allow—fashion and refashion these according to their own judgment. And even if these sometimes sound like great mysteries, they can prove or evince nothing; indeed, according to the words of **Gregory** <note>Likely Pope Gregory the Great.</note>, one may despise them with the same ease with which they are asserted. **Rabanus the Monk** <note>Rabanus Maurus (c. 780–856), a Benedictine abbot and scholar known for his "In honorem sanctae crucis," which used complex word-grids and images.</note> fashioned many things with a similar artifice, but using Latin characters and verses, inserting various images which, read in any direction through any lines of the surface and figures, announce some sacred mystery representing the histories depicted there; such things are even wrung from profane literature—

<summary>The author critiques the Jewish Cabala, arguing that while Moses and the prophets performed true miracles, the modern "art" of Cabala is merely a superstitious play of letter-manipulation that lacks the saving power found only in the name of Jesus.</summary>
<keywords>Cabala, Moses, miracles, Jewish mysticism, theurgy, Jesus, Rabanus Maurus, allegory, Hebrew language, divine names</keywords>

# ON THE CABALA

<page-num>360</page-num>

No one is ignorant of the fact that such things can be done, if they have read the poems of Valeria Proba <note>A 4th-century Roman poet who rearranged Virgil's lines to tell the story of the Bible</note> composed of snippets from the songs of Virgil; all of these are merely the speculations of idle men. However, as far as the performance of miracles is concerned, I think none of you is so stiff-necked as to believe that there is any art or science to be had concerning them.

<margin>What the Cabala is</margin>
Therefore, this "Cabala" <note>original: "cabala"; referring here to Jewish mystical tradition involving letter and number symbolism</note> of the Jews is nothing other than a most pernicious superstition. By it, they collect, divide, and transfer words, names, and letters placed scattered throughout the scripture according to their own whim. Making one thing out of another, they tear apart the limbs of truth, constructing speeches, inductions, and parables here and there from their own fictions. They wish to fit the oracles of God to these fictions, defaming the scriptures and saying that their own figments consist of them. They misrepresent the law of God, and through impudently extorted calculations of words, syllables, letters, and numbers, they attempt to introduce violent and blasphemous proofs for their own faithlessness. Furthermore, puffed up by these trifles, they boast that they find and know the ineffable mysteries of God and secrets which are above scripture; through these, they do not blush to lie with great audacity, claiming that they even prophesy and perform virtues and miracles. But it happens to them as it did to Aesop’s dog, who, leaving the bread behind and gaping at its shadow, lost his food. Thus this faithless and stiff-necked race of men, always occupied in the shadows of scripture and making an assault upon those vanities with their artificial but superstitious Cabala, loses the bread of eternal life, and, fed upon empty names, loses the word of truth.

<margin>Note</margin>
From this Jewish leaven of Cabalistic superstition, I believe, came the Ophites, Gnostics, and Valentinian heretics <note>Early Christian sects often accused of blending philosophy and mysticism with scripture</note>. They too, along with their disciples, devised a certain Greek Cabala, perverting all the mysteries of the Christian faith and dragging them with heretical depravity toward Greek letters and numbers. From these they construct a body which they call "Truth," teaching that without these mysteries of letters and numbers, the truth cannot be found in the Gospel writings. They claim the scriptures are varied and in some places contradictory, written full of parables so that "those seeing may not see, and those hearing may not hear, and those understanding may not understand," but are set forth for the blind and wandering according to the capacity of their blindness and error. They believe the sincere truth lying hidden beneath them was entrusted only to the "perfected," not through writings, but through the successive pronunciation of the living voice. They claim this is that alphabetic and arithmetical theology which Christ secretly manifested to the apostles, and which Paul says he speaks only among the perfect. For since these are the highest mysteries, they were neither written down nor should be written, but kept in silence among the wise, guarding them with themselves in secret. But among them, no one is "wise" unless he knows how to manufacture the greatest monsters of heresy.

### ON ILLUSIONS

But let us return to magic, a small part of which is the craft of illusions <term>praestigium: a trick or deception of the senses</term>, that is, of deceptions which occur only according to appearance. By these, magi produce phantasms and many miracles through the tricks of jugglers...

# ON ILLUSIONS.

They play with frauds and send dreams, which is achieved not only through goetic <note>original: "goëticis" — referring to low magic or sorcery involving the summoning of spirits</note> incantations, imprecations, and the deceits of demons, but also through certain fumigating vapors, lights, love potions, eye-salves, bindings, and suspensions. Furthermore, it is performed through rings, images, mirrors, and similar medicines and instruments of the magical art, by natural and celestial power. Many things are also done with a ready subtlety and industry of the hands, the kind we see daily performed by actors and jugglers, whom we therefore call "hand-wise" <note>original: "chiro-sophos" — from the Greek for skilled with hands</note>. There exist books on this craft of illusions by Hermes and certain others. We also read that a certain very crowded banquet was customarily shown to guests by Paphates <note>likely a reference to Pasetes, a legendary magician</note>, a most expert illusionist, which vanished again when he pleased, leaving all the guests mocked by hunger and thirst. We read that Numa Pompilius also used illusions of this kind. Even the most learned Pythagoras occasionally practiced this trick: he would write whatever he pleased in blood on a mirror, and having turned it toward the orb of the full moon, he showed the things inscribed on the disk of the moon to someone standing behind him. To this also belongs whatever is read concerning the transformations of men, celebrated by poets, believed by historians, and asserted by some Christian theologians, and moreover by the Sacred Scriptures. Thus men appear as
<column-break/>
donkeys or horses or other animals to fascinated eyes, or when the medium is disturbed, and this by natural art. Sometimes these things are also done by good and evil spirits, or at the prayers of the good by God himself, as we read in the Sacred Scriptures concerning the prophet Elisha, when he was besieged by the army of the king of Syria surrounding Dothan. Truly, these things cannot deceive eyes that are pure and opened by God; thus that woman, who was judged by the common people to be a beast of burden, appeared to Hilarion <note>St. Hilarion, a 4th-century hermit</note> not as a beast, but as the woman she was. Therefore, those things which happen in this way according to appearance are called illusions <note>original: "praestigia"</note>. But those things which are done by the art of those who transform or transfer—such as concerning Nebuchadnezzar, or harvests moved to other fields—we have spoken of these above. Truly, concerning this art of illusions, Iamblichus <note>A Neoplatonist philosopher</note> says: "Those who are under illusion or fascinated imagine things which, beyond the imagination, have no truth of action or essence." For the end of such a craft is not to create simply, but to offer images up to the point of appearance, of which soon no trace remains. Now, therefore, from these things which have been said,
<margin>Note</margin>
it is clear that magic is nothing other than a complex of idolatry, astrology, and superstitious medicine. And now also from the magicians a great crowd of heretics has arisen in the Church, who just as Jannes and Mambres <note>The Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses</note> resisted Moses, so they resisted the apostolic truth. Their prince was Simon the Samaritan <note>Simon Magus</note>, who at Rome under Claudius Caesar was gifted a statue because of this art, with this inscription: *To Simon the Holy God*. Clement, Eusebius, and Irenaeus narrate his blasphemies copiously. From this Simon, as if from a nursery of all heresies, through many successions the monstrous Ophites, the shameful Gnostics, the impious Valentinians, Cerdonians, Marcionites, Montanists, and many other heretics came forth, for the sake of profit and empty glory, lying against God, [bringing] no utility,

<summary>This page defines "praestigia" (illusions) as sensory deceptions caused by natural means, sleight of hand, or spiritual influence, distinguishing them from actual physical transformation. It concludes by linking the history of magic to the rise of early Christian heresies, specifically citing Simon Magus as a primary source of error.</summary>

<meta>This page marks the conclusion of Heinrich Cornelius Agrippa’s "De Occulta Philosophia" (Three Books of Occult Philosophy). The tone is one of formal retraction, a common practice for authors of controversial works in the 16th century to avoid charges of heresy.</meta>

# ON DECEPTIONS

<margin>Those who follow the Kabbalah <note>original: "Cabala qui"; the author is likely referring to those who misuse mystical traditions for sorcery.</note></margin>
...neither providing benefits to men, but rather deceiving them, and leading them into destruction and error; and those who believe in them shall be confounded in the judgment of God. Truly, while I was still a young man, I wrote three books of considerable volume concerning magic, which I titled *On Occult Philosophy*. In these books, whatever errors I committed through the curiosity of my youth, I now—being more cautious—wish to take back by recanting with this "palinodia" <note>A "palinodia" is a formal poem or statement in which a writer retracts a view expressed in a former poem or text.</note>. For I once wasted a great deal of time and resources on these vanities. At last, I have gained this much: that I know by what arguments others ought to be discouraged from this destruction. For whoever presumes to divine and prophesy—not in the truth, nor in the power of God, but in the delusion of demons, according to the operation of evil spirits—and those who practice magic vanities, exorcisms, incantations, love potions, "agogima" <note>original: "agogima"; a term for spells intended to lead or draw a person to the magician, often for romantic or sexual purposes.</note>, and other demoniacal works and frauds of idolatry, boasting that they perform miracles by showing off deceptions and phantasms that soon vanish: all these shall be destined to be tortured in eternal fires along with Jannes and Mambres <note>Biblical figures traditionally identified as the Egyptian magicians who opposed Moses.</note> and Simon Magus <note>A figure from the Acts of the Apostles who attempted to buy the power of the Holy Spirit, giving rise to the term "simony."</note>.
